literature_notes: All three ledger lines were examined carefully. L1 (PMC10684670) reports a C-terminal FLAG tag on full-length, membrane-anchored B7-H6 in 293T and U87 cells, with confirmed surface trafficking. However, NCR3LG1/B7-H6 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein (signal peptide 1-24, extracellular 25-264, TM 265-282, intracellular 283-454); its C-terminus (residue 454) is intracellular. The tag is tolerated but faces the cytoplasm — it is recorded in other_positions. L2 (PMC13282662) describes a chimeric construct named FLAG-OX40L-B7H6-EGFP. OX40L is a type II TM protein; the FLAG tag sits at the N-terminus of OX40L in this multi-component fusion, and no residue of B7-H6 is named as the tag insertion point. The tag position on B7-H6 is entirely unstated, disqualifying this line under the rule against plasmids with unstated tag position. L3 (PMC13282662) is flow cytometry confirming surface expression of the L2 construct; it names no insertion residue and is antibody detection of the protein, not an epitope-tag insertion site. No ledger line supports an extracellular surface tag site with a pinnable position on NCR3LG1.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal FLAG (and 2×Strep-3×FLAG) tag on full-length B7-H6 is tolerated and the protein traffics to the cell surface, but residue 454 (Q) is the intracellular C-terminus of this type I TM protein — the tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular space.
